errors.text: The hypothesis asserts intrinsic entropy-based stability and sluggish diffusion, whereas the target system exhibits active diffusion, surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, melting, and evaporation.
The proposed materials, sizes, and structures do not reconstruct the relevant sub-10 nm equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles with multi-twinned or icosahedral FCC structures.

The falsification experiment is performed at 0.7 Tm, above the hypothesis's own proposed 0.6 Tm instability threshold, so observing clustering or phase separation is a prediction of the hypothesis rather than a clean falsification.
Evidence E2 concerns thermal conductivity and phonon transport; it does not establish that SRO percolation pathways enhance atomic diffusion.
The proposed SRO-driven phase decomposition mechanism omits the decisive nanoparticle mechanism: element-specific surface-energy differences and shape-dependent surface segregation.
